sections.title: The Ministry of the New Covenant
observations: In this section, Paul contrasts the old covenant, represented by the law given to Moses, with the new covenant established through Christ. He emphasizes that the new covenant is not written on tablets of stone but on the hearts of believers, signifying a transformative relationship with God.

Paul argues that the ministry of the new covenant is more glorious than the old, as it brings life and righteousness rather than condemnation. This highlights the superiority of the gospel and the work of the Holy Spirit in the lives of believers.

sections.title: The Glory of the New Covenant
observations: Paul reflects on the glory that accompanied Moses when he received the law, which was so radiant that he had to wear a veil. However, he points out that this glory was fading, whereas the glory of the new covenant is permanent and surpasses the old.
This section emphasizes that the new covenant brings a lasting transformation and a direct relationship with God, where believers can behold His glory and be changed into His likeness.

sections.title: The Boldness of the New Covenant Ministry
observations: In this part, Paul speaks about the boldness that comes from the new covenant. Unlike Moses, who veiled his face, Paul encourages believers to approach God with unveiled faces, reflecting the glory of the Lord.
This boldness is rooted in the confidence that comes from the Spirit, allowing believers to proclaim the gospel without fear or hesitation.

importantVerses.commentary: Paul emphasizes that believers are a letter from Christ, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, highlighting the personal and transformative nature of the new covenant.
Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. This verse encapsulates the essence of the new covenant, which liberates believers from the bondage of sin and the law.
We all, with unveiled faces, reflect the Lord's glory and are being transformed into His image. This verse speaks to the ongoing sanctification process in the life of a believer.

questions: What does it mean for believers to be a letter from Christ, and how does this shape our understanding of our identity in Him?
How does the concept of freedom in the Spirit challenge our understanding of the law and our daily lives as Christians?
In what ways can we reflect the glory of the Lord in our lives, and what does that transformation look like practically?
